coachMessages.text: The undercut: a lower threat kills the upper threat because gravity fills bottom-up.

slides.infoProse: Red has a three-in-a-row at row 0 (columns 0–2) and Yellow has one at row 1 (columns 0–2). Both would complete with column 3. The lower threat (Red, row 0) fills first because of gravity, killing Yellow's threat at row 1.

coachMessages.text: The undercut only works when the lower threat is on a different parity row than the upper threat. Same-parity threats coexist (T4 rule).

slides.infoProse: Both threats are at even-indexed rows (0 and 2), which means they're on the same parity. The lower one does not kill the upper one — both must be blocked separately. This is the T4 (same-parity) rule.
